title: Partial-object stitching, ordering guarantees, and tool idempotency acceptance criteria
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: Define concrete acceptance criteria for handling partial structured output (objects emitted across a stream) and the semantics of tool/function calls when streams are interrupted, reordered, or retried. Scope: frontend API contract (response envelope and headers), runtime reconciliation logic (stitching fragments, detecting duplicates, ordering constraints), and observable signals for client operators. Out of scope: model training/evaluation changes, persistent storage design beyond checkpoints. This ticket clarifies requirements, produces a small PRD, and defines test harnesses for QA and e2e validation.
acceptance_criteria: Schema handshake: The first emission in any streamed response must include a metadata frame that declares the output schema version (v1 or v2) and a unique stream_id. Consumers must be able to validate subsequent partial objects against that declared schema without requiring additional schema fetches.

Deterministic reassembly: Given a sequence of partial object frames with monotonic sequence numbers, the runtime must deterministically reassemble the final object such that reassembly is independent of transient delivery timing. Reassembly succeeds when the set of required keys (per schema) are present or an explicit 'final' flag is received.

Out-of-order tolerance: Runtimes must accept partial frames arriving up to 3 seconds out of order and reorder them before emitting to the client. If frames are missing after a configurable window (default 5s), the runtime must emit a progress frame indicating missing sequence ranges and either wait for retry or apply the configured degradation policy.

Idempotent tool-calls: Any tool/function call invoked by the model that is persisted by the runtime must include a unique call_id. Retries with the same call_id must be treated idempotently: duplicate calls must not trigger side effects in downstream integrations (client infra must support idempotency keys and 409 semantics where applicable).

Partial failure modes: Define three canonical error modes: transient (retryable by runtime), permanent (surface error and abort stream), and resumable (checkpoint exists, can resume from last ack). Acceptance requires documented mapping from transport errors to these modes and automated tests covering each mapping.

Checkpointing and resume: For streams that include long-running tool handoffs, the runtime must emit checkpoints every N significant frames (configurable; default N=10). A resumed stream with a valid checkpoint token must not re-execute tool calls that were already confirmed by downstream systems.

Monotonic observability: Each emitted frame must include monotonically increasing local offsets and vector of telemetry tags (model_version, route, region, call_id). Console dashboards should be able to reconstruct a stream and display missing ranges and reassembly status within the trace view.

Backward compatibility: When schema version changes are introduced, runtime must support v1 payloads for 90 days and provide a migration warning in the console. New fields in v2 must be optional for that window to prevent silent failures.

Client-level contract: SDKs must expose a stable API that returns partial objects as they become reassembled and expose explicit events for 'checkpoint', 'resume', 'degraded-result', and 'tool-confirmation'. Documentation examples for Node and Python must be provided in the PRD.

E2E test coverage: Acceptance requires an automated e2e suite that simulates network partitions, duplicate frames, out-of-order delivery, and tool retries. Tests must assert final-object equality and that side effects (tool calls) occurred exactly-once when call_id is present.

Performance SLOs under streaming: Under normal load (p50 latency profile), reassembly and emission of partial objects should add no more than 25ms median overhead compared to equivalent non-streamed requests. Telemetry must flag regressions above 2x baseline.

User-visible fallback: If the runtime degrades (missing frames beyond configured window), the client-facing response must include a human-readable 'partial_result_reason' and guidance on retry/resume UX; product copy to be reviewed by UX writing team.
updates: 2026-02-19: Initial scoping meeting with Eng (Liam), SDK (Priya), and Platform (Marcus). Agreed to target Node/Python SDK behaviors first.
2026-02-24: Drafted PRD outline and linked example payloads (see links). Liam to propose concrete header names and checkpoint token format.
2026-02-28: Engineering feedback: prefer sequence numbers + bitmap for missing ranges rather than range lists to reduce payload size. Document updated to reflect decision.
2026-03-04: Security review request raised (ticket SEC-3401). Identified KMS requirement for call_id provenance in Private deployments.

2026-03-08: QA added tests for duplicate frames and idempotent call semantics. Ran initial e2e harness against staging runtime; two non-blocking failures observed (ordering window too small) and retuned windows to 5s.
2026-03-12: PRD reviewed by PM and Eng leads; awaiting legal review for downstream vendor idempotency clauses. Preparing GH PR for SDK surface.
implementation_notes: Engineering to implement in three phases: 1) schema handshake + basic reassembly (runtime), 2) checkpointing and idempotent call propagation (runtime + integrations), 3) SDK events and console telemetry. Use feature flag 'partial_stream_v1' for gradual rollout. Runtime will adopt a small on-wire header 'X-RW-Stream: <stream_id>:<seq>' and a compact bitmap for missing ranges.
testing_plan: QA to author deterministic unit tests for reassembly logic and integrate network-fault simulator into runner. E2E harness to run nightly against canary and produce regression diffs. Include load test that measures 25ms overhead target.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: downstream integrations may not respect idempotency keys. Mitigation: provide a compatibility shim in Dedicated docs and gating for Private installs; surface list of known non-idempotent vendors to Solutions Engineering.
rollback_plan: If stability regressions appear in canary, disable feature flag 'partial_stream_v1' and fall back to atomic (non-streamed) responses for affected routes. Maintain telemetry to detect and alert on rollback-triggering errors.
